safety.title: Safety Guidelines
safety.disclaimer: Always consult your doctor before starting a new exercise program. Stop immediately if you feel pain, dizziness, or shortness of breath. Use a sturdy chair for seated exercises. Go at your own pace.

tai_chi_cloud_hands.name: Cloud Hands (Seated)
tai_chi_cloud_hands.description: A gentle, flowing arm movement that improves upper body mobility and relaxation.
steps: Sit tall in your chair with feet flat on the floor, hands resting on your thighs
Slowly raise your right hand to shoulder height, palm facing left
Sweep your right hand across your body to the left in a smooth arc
As your right hand lowers, begin raising your left hand
Continue alternating hands in a flowing motion for 8-10 repetitions
Breathe slowly and naturally throughout the movement
tai_chi_cloud_hands.safetyTip: Keep movements slow and controlled. Do not twist your torso beyond comfort.

tai_chi_brush_knee.name: Brush Knee (Seated)
tai_chi_brush_knee.description: A classic Tai Chi movement adapted for seated practice, improving arm coordination and flexibility.
steps: Sit upright with feet flat on the floor, shoulder-width apart
Raise your right hand beside your ear, palm facing forward
Simultaneously, bring your left hand to hip level, palm facing down
Push your right hand forward while sweeping your left hand across your knee
Return to the starting position and switch sides
Repeat 6-8 times on each side, breathing naturally
tai_chi_brush_knee.safetyTip: Keep your back straight against the chair. Move your arms only, not your torso.

tai_chi_repulse_monkey.name: Repulse Monkey (Seated)
tai_chi_repulse_monkey.description: A backward stepping movement adapted for seated practice, building arm strength and coordination.
steps: Sit tall with feet flat, arms relaxed at your sides
Extend your right arm forward at shoulder height, palm up
Bring your left hand behind you near your hip, palm up
Pull your right hand back toward your hip while pushing your left hand forward
Your palms turn over during the transition — right palm faces up as it retreats
Continue alternating for 6-8 repetitions on each side
Maintain slow, steady breathing throughout
tai_chi_repulse_monkey.safetyTip: Focus on smooth transitions between arms. Do not rush the movements.

tai_chi_wave_hands.name: Wave Hands Like Clouds (Seated)
tai_chi_wave_hands.description: A flowing side-to-side movement that promotes relaxation and gentle spinal rotation.
steps: Sit comfortably with feet flat, hands on your lap
Raise both hands to chest height, palms facing your body
Slowly turn your upper body to the right, sweeping both hands right
As you turn back to center, let your hands float across
Continue turning to the left, sweeping hands in the same direction
Repeat 8-10 times, alternating sides with gentle breathing
tai_chi_wave_hands.safetyTip: Rotate from the waist gently. Stop if you feel any discomfort in your back.

tai_chi_golden_rooster.name: Golden Rooster Stands (Seated)
tai_chi_golden_rooster.description: An advanced seated balance exercise that strengthens the legs and improves stability.
steps: Sit at the front edge of a sturdy chair, back straight
Place both hands on your thighs for support
Slowly lift your right knee upward as high as comfortable
At the same time, raise your left hand to shoulder height, palm open
Hold the position for 3-5 seconds, focusing on balance
Slowly lower your knee and hand back to the starting position
Repeat on the other side. Do 5-6 repetitions per side
tai_chi_golden_rooster.safetyTip: Keep one hand on the chair seat if needed for extra stability. Do not lean backward.

stretch_neck_rolls.name: Gentle Neck Rolls
stretch_neck_rolls.description: Releases tension in the neck and upper shoulders. Can be done seated or standing.
steps: Sit or stand tall, shoulders relaxed and down
Slowly drop your chin toward your chest
Roll your head gently to the right, bringing your ear toward your shoulder
Continue rolling your head back (look up gently) then to the left
Complete a full slow circle, then reverse direction
stretch_neck_rolls.safetyTip: Move very slowly. If you feel dizziness or pain, reduce the range of motion.

stretch_shoulder_shrugs.name: Shoulder Shrugs
stretch_shoulder_shrugs.description: Relieves shoulder and upper back tension. Simple and effective for desk or chair sitting.
steps: Sit or stand with arms relaxed at your sides
Slowly raise both shoulders toward your ears
Hold the raised position for 3-5 seconds
Release and let your shoulders drop back down naturally
Repeat 8-10 times, breathing out as you release
stretch_shoulder_shrugs.safetyTip: Do not force the shrug higher than comfortable. Keep your neck relaxed.

stretch_seated_hamstring.name: Seated Hamstring Stretch
stretch_seated_hamstring.description: Stretches the back of the thighs while seated. Helps maintain leg flexibility.
steps: Sit at the front edge of your chair
Extend your right leg forward with heel on the floor, toes pointing up
Keep your left foot flat on the floor, knee bent
With a straight back, slowly hinge forward from your hips
Reach toward your right toes until you feel a gentle stretch behind your thigh
Hold for 15-20 seconds, then switch legs
stretch_seated_hamstring.safetyTip: Do not bounce. Keep your back straight — the stretch comes from the hip hinge, not rounding your back.

stretch_ankle_circles.name: Ankle Circles
stretch_ankle_circles.description: Improves ankle mobility and circulation in the lower legs.
steps: Sit comfortably with feet flat on the floor
Lift your right foot slightly off the floor
Slowly rotate your ankle clockwise in large circles
Do 10 circles, then reverse to counter-clockwise
Switch to your left foot and repeat
stretch_ankle_circles.safetyTip: Support yourself by holding the sides of the chair. Move slowly and smoothly.

stretch_wrist_hands.name: Wrist & Hand Stretches
stretch_wrist_hands.description: Relieves stiffness in the hands and wrists. Especially helpful for arthritis.
steps: Extend your right arm forward, palm facing up
Use your left hand to gently pull your right fingers downward
Hold for 10-15 seconds, feeling the stretch along your forearm
Flip your right palm to face down and gently press fingers toward you
Hold for 10-15 seconds, then switch hands
Finish by making gentle fists and releasing 10 times
stretch_wrist_hands.safetyTip: Be gentle — wrist stretches should not cause pain. Ease off if you feel tingling.

balance_weight_shift.name: Weight Shifting
balance_weight_shift.description: A beginner balance exercise that teaches weight distribution awareness.
steps: Stand behind a sturdy chair, holding the back for support
Place your feet hip-width apart
Slowly shift your weight onto your right foot
Hold for 5-10 seconds, feeling the balance on one side
Shift your weight to the left foot and hold
balance_weight_shift.safetyTip: Always keep the chair within reach. Do not let go of the chair until you feel confident.

balance_standing_march.name: Standing March
balance_standing_march.description: Improves balance and leg strength by marching in place with high knees.
steps: Stand behind a chair, holding the back lightly for balance
Lift your right knee as high as comfortable
Hold briefly, then slowly lower your foot back down
Lift your left knee in the same way
Continue alternating for 20 steps (10 each side)
balance_standing_march.safetyTip: Keep your chest upright. Use the chair as much as needed for stability.

balance_single_leg.name: Single Leg Stand
balance_single_leg.description: Classic balance exercise. Stand on one leg with chair support for safety.
steps: Stand next to a sturdy chair, one hand on the back
Slowly lift your right foot a few inches off the floor
Try to balance on your left leg for 10-15 seconds
Lower your foot and rest briefly
Switch to the other leg
As you improve, try using just your fingertips on the chair
balance_single_leg.safetyTip: Keep a firm grip on the chair. Never close your eyes during this exercise.

balance_heel_toe_walk.name: Heel-to-Toe Walk
balance_heel_toe_walk.description: Walking in a straight line placing heel to toe, building balance and coordination.
steps: Stand near a wall or counter for support if needed
Place your right foot directly in front of your left, heel touching toes
Focus on a point ahead for balance
Step forward placing your left heel against your right toes
Continue for 15-20 steps in a straight line
Turn around carefully and repeat back
balance_heel_toe_walk.safetyTip: Stay close to a wall or have someone nearby. Move slowly and deliberately.

balance_tandem_stance.name: Tandem Stance Hold
balance_tandem_stance.description: An advanced static balance challenge — holding heel-to-toe position for extended time.
steps: Stand near a wall with one hand lightly touching it
Place one foot directly in front of the other, heel to toe
Try to hold this position for 30 seconds
Focus your eyes on a fixed point for stability
Switch which foot is in front and repeat
As you improve, reduce hand contact with the wall
balance_tandem_stance.safetyTip: Have a support surface always within arm's reach. Stop if you feel dizzy.

strength_chair_squats.name: Chair Squats
strength_chair_squats.description: Sit-to-stand movement using a chair. Builds leg strength for daily activities.
steps: Sit at the front edge of a sturdy chair, feet hip-width apart
Cross your arms over your chest or extend them forward
Lean slightly forward and press through your heels to stand up
Pause briefly at the top, standing tall
Slowly lower yourself back to the seated position
Repeat 8-10 times. Rest if needed between sets
strength_chair_squats.safetyTip: Use your hands on the chair arms if needed. Do not let your knees extend past your toes.

strength_seated_leg_raise.name: Seated Leg Raises
strength_seated_leg_raise.description: Strengthens the quadriceps while seated. Great for knee stability.
steps: Sit tall in your chair, feet flat on the floor
Slowly straighten your right leg out in front of you
Hold the raised position for 3-5 seconds, squeezing your thigh
Slowly lower your leg back to the floor
Repeat 10 times, then switch to the left leg
strength_seated_leg_raise.safetyTip: Hold the sides of the chair for support. Move slowly without jerking.

strength_wall_pushups.name: Wall Push-Ups
strength_wall_pushups.description: A standing push-up variation using a wall. Builds chest and arm strength safely.
steps: Stand facing a wall, about arm's length away
Place your palms flat on the wall at shoulder height and width
Slowly bend your elbows, leaning your body toward the wall
Your body should stay straight from head to heels
Push yourself back to the starting position
Repeat 8-12 times
strength_wall_pushups.safetyTip: Keep your feet firmly planted. Do not arch your lower back.

strength_arm_curls.name: Arm Curls (Water Bottles)
strength_arm_curls.description: Bicep curls using water bottles as weights. Builds arm strength for carrying groceries.
steps: Sit or stand with a water bottle (500ml-1L) in each hand
Arms at your sides, palms facing forward
Slowly curl both bottles toward your shoulders
Squeeze briefly at the top
Slowly lower back to the starting position
Repeat 10-12 times for 2 sets
strength_arm_curls.safetyTip: Use a comfortable weight. If water bottles are too heavy, start with empty ones.

strength_calf_raises.name: Standing Calf Raises
strength_calf_raises.description: Strengthens the calves for better walking stability and balance.
steps: Stand behind a chair, holding the back for support
Place feet hip-width apart
Slowly rise up onto your toes, lifting your heels as high as you can
Hold at the top for 2-3 seconds
Slowly lower your heels back to the floor
Repeat 12-15 times for 2 sets
strength_calf_raises.safetyTip: Keep a firm grip on the chair. Control the movement — do not bounce.

cardio_seated_march.name: Seated Marching
cardio_seated_march.description: A gentle cardio exercise done while sitting. Elevates heart rate safely.
steps: Sit tall in your chair, feet flat on the floor
Lift your right knee up toward your chest
Lower it back down, then lift your left knee
Continue alternating like a marching motion
Swing your arms naturally as you march
cardio_seated_march.safetyTip: Start slowly and increase speed gradually. Stop if you feel breathless.

cardio_arm_circles.name: Arm Circles
cardio_arm_circles.description: Seated or standing arm circles that warm up shoulders and get blood flowing.
steps: Sit or stand with arms extended out to the sides at shoulder height
Make small forward circles with both arms
Gradually increase the circle size over 15 seconds
Reverse direction and make backward circles
Do 30 seconds in each direction
cardio_arm_circles.safetyTip: Lower your arms if your shoulders fatigue. Keep breathing throughout.

cardio_step_in_place.name: Step-in-Place
cardio_step_in_place.description: Standing march with more energy. A moderate cardio exercise to build endurance.
steps: Stand behind a chair for support if needed
March in place, lifting your knees higher with each step
Add arm pumping — swing opposite arm with each step
Maintain a steady rhythm for 2-3 minutes
Slow down gradually, then rest for 30 seconds
Repeat for 2-3 intervals
cardio_step_in_place.safetyTip: Keep the chair nearby. If you feel winded, slow down or switch to seated marching.

cardio_seated_jacks.name: Seated Jumping Jacks
cardio_seated_jacks.description: A chair-friendly version of jumping jacks. Works arms and legs together for cardio.
steps: Sit tall in your chair, feet together, arms at your sides
Simultaneously spread your legs apart and raise your arms overhead
Bring your legs back together and lower your arms
Continue at a comfortable pace for 30 seconds
Rest for 15 seconds, then repeat for 3 rounds
Coordinate your breathing: inhale as you open, exhale as you close
cardio_seated_jacks.safetyTip: Stay seated firmly in the chair. Reduce the range of arm movement if your shoulders are stiff.

cardio_side_steps.name: Standing Side Steps
cardio_side_steps.description: Lateral stepping for cardio and hip mobility. An advanced standing exercise.
steps: Stand with feet together, arms at your sides or on your hips
Step your right foot out to the right side
Bring your left foot to meet it
Take 4-5 steps to the right, then reverse to the left
Add arm raises as you step — lift arms out to the sides and lower them
Continue for 2-3 minutes at a steady pace
cardio_side_steps.safetyTip: Ensure your exercise area is clear of obstacles. Stay near a counter or wall.
